sources.title: OSWorld 2.0 (Yuan et al.)
sources.role: Discovery-bounded source used for factual verification

claims.text: 108 long-horizon workflows (median 1.6 human-hours); tool-call scale is config-bound: Claude Opus 4.7 with maximum thinking in single-action setting averages 318.4 calls over the 108 tasks vs ~30 in OSWorld 1.0; challenge phenomena incl. streaming interaction, dynamic environments, cross-source reasoning, implicit-state inference, visual-spatial precision; authentic artifacts + stateful user profiles + safety reports; best 500-step config is separate: Claude Opus 4.8 max-thinking batched 20.6% binary / 54.8% partial (481.8 calls); GPT-5.5 token-efficient plateau ~13%.
claims.context: Full-paper abstract (178KB body, abstract-depth consumed); v2 July 2026; all numbers author-measured at report date.

claims.text: Thesis shift: failures move from GUI control/coding to constraint-tracking, mid-task information arrival, implicit-state recovery, and verification skipping — the state-management bottleneck.

limitations.text: Author-measured model results; strictest binding in volume required per use (model+thinking+tool+steps+release).
limitations.context: Evidence boundary retained for downstream editorial use.

targets.finding: Complete OSWorld 2.0 paper body consumed via arXiv HTML (178KB text): workflow design, phenomena taxonomy, binary/partial results, thesis shift verified; v2 status confirmed.
Strict binding fields recorded in claims; per-use binding belongs to later stages.
